doc.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: The festival and party circuit, and a German tour
summary: The 50 to 100 players on the jazz party circuit, an eight-week German bus tour, and audiences in Europe versus the US.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well when you describe leaving that situation to go on the circuit, can you describe to me what circuit exists now for you?

Well I think there’s a handful of about 50 to 100 guys who are traveling around the world doing different jazz oriented things within the spectrum of the music that we’re listening to right now, doing these kind of jazz parties, festivals, here in the States and in Europe. And you might see my name on one or two of them and you’ll see somebody else’s name on two or three, but next year you might see that reversed. And so that’s basically what I’m talking about. Like I’ve done a festival or a party where I’m there one year and then I don’t come back for a couple of years, and they’ve got Kenny or they’ve got Bob Wilber or they’ve got Abe Most or they’ve got — they always get one or two clarinetists — Harry Allen does tons of them. Plus doing different tours of people who bring bands over for tours in Europe and so forth and so on. There’s a couple of guys in Germany. Butch © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
and I were like eight weeks in Germany a couple of years ago, on the bus doing one- nighters all through the country.

Well no, it was like one of these all-star bands — it was Bob Haggart and Butch and Johnny Varro and Bob Havens and myself, Ed Polcer. I can’t remember all the guys on the band. But it was about an eight or nine piece band.
Any reaction to the music over there?

Yeah generally you get a much more enthusiastic reaction than you do here in the States. Plus you will find the ages of the audience are much more diversified than they are here. As a general rule you don’t see a lot of people my age, or under the age of 60 at a lot of these festivals and parties that I do here in the States, but you do in Europe.
It is rather a shame. It concerns me. Because I wonder what’s going to happen say 20 or 25 years from now.
